acceptance.assertion: The bottleneck is reproduced from current state rather than historical summary.
The diagnosis names causal evidence, uncertainty, and excluded explanations.
The outcome is either a tested repair or one bounded canonical follow-up.

approval.note: Bounded supply fallback. Re-read live state, preserve foreign work, and stop when the stated scope or evidence no longer matches.

goal: Diagnose one current throughput or reliability bottleneck and produce either a bounded repair or a canonically registered follow-up with exact blockers.

does_not_establish: permission to bypass current leases or open-PR guards

acceptance_evidence.diagnosis-1: The coordinated run was created from the then-current Bureau/PR state, later terminalized succeeded, and its live pickup readback now reports coordination_blocking=false rather than inferring completion from historical summaries.
acceptance_evidence.diagnosis-2: The diagnosis isolated the missing canonical Bureau binding around Grabowski PR #677 and did not take over foreign work; the resulting bounded follow-up was registered separately as OPERATOR-INTEGRATION-LOOP-V1-FB-DIAGNOSIS-EA32ADE502.
acceptance_evidence.diagnosis-3: The canonical follow-up task EA32ADE502 is present on Bureau main through merged PR #1729. Grabowski PR #677 is merged and the deployed runtime now serves merge commit c59c64da66ca505816c4b9cb9217f0581538ebaa with valid integrity. A fresh transport bootstrap executed an exact mutating resource acquisition while client allow_mutation was omitted, and a nested branch-publish negative control with allow_mutation omitted was blocked before effect.

does_not_establish: future runtime correctness after later Grabowski deployments
automatic claimability of unrelated Bureau tasks
permission to release or mutate foreign resources

title: Diagnose one current Bureau bottleneck
